author: tomas
text: Breaker opening rule: >=3 timeouts in a 60 s window from >=2 distinct turns, and timeouts >= half the window's answered probes; a success no longer resets a count; connection error opens at once; half-open trial unchanged. Per-turn cap: a turn with 3 timeouts in the window skips the store for the rest of that window. Why: AC1-3 with the fewest knobs; an outage across two turns opens after the same 3 timeouts as today.

author: nils
text: sc-365 cause check: NOT the _acap cap for BKNtypgnhrxXvj84. Evidence: livecheck.py --facts notes fights 1-2 are timed M+ keys (Den of Nalorakk is fight 2, kill=true, encounterID set) and the last boss kill is fight 32 Ula'tek; ~32 fights x ~400 chars is ~13k chars, far under the 60k cap. The tool gives no times and no kill marker, so 'last boss kill' is the model's guess over kill=true rows, and an M+ key run looks like a boss kill. The cap is a second, real path on long nights (100+ trash pulls). Fix covers both: explicit last_kill + per-boss summary outside the capped list, keystone runs excluded.

Keystone (M+) runs are excluded from last_kill and bosses: a key run is a dungeon, not a boss kill (it caused the live miss). Fights with keystoneLevel get that key in the fights list.

author: ansel
text: Tombstone overflow (sc-353): keep the 1024 cap; when an entry still inside the 10-min window is evicted by overflow, its time raises a per-process floor: any report fetch requested at or before the floor is treated as stale (not stored). Codes over 32 chars aren't tombstoned (never servable). Why: memory stays fixed (1024 entries + one timestamp) and the real tombstone's protection can never be flushed; the worst a flood does is skip storing in-flight fetches (availability of the store, not a leak). Rejected: growing past the cap inside the window (bound then rests only on the WCL rate).

author: ansel
text: Signals on a full queue (sc-353): ReportGone items bypass the item/byte caps (tiny, one per WCL answer). A dropped summary of our own query is salvaged: its private and null-entry codes are parsed (off the loop when big, as today) and queued as a ReportGone with the summary's fetched_at - exactly what the private path already does. The body itself is still dropped, so memory per signal is codes only. Why: never drop the signal while keeping the byte bound meaningful.

author: ansel
text: Own-summary flag (sc-354): new raw_fetches.own_summary boolean NOT NULL default false, set in upsert_raw_fetch when the query text equals REPORT_SUMMARY or report_summaries_query(n) and the exact codes equal the stored codes. Migration 0021 backfills with the old lookup's rule (_flight_key re-derived from our query text + stored params, exact codes == report_codes), so flagged rows = rows the old lookup accepted.

author: ansel
text: Lookup driver (sc-354): drop the fetched_at >= since bound. Candidates on Postgres = own-summary rows whose report_codes ?| (codes granted to the tenant since 'since' UNION public codes checked since 'since'), via a partial GIN index WHERE own_summary; then the unchanged fetch_visible_clause, newest first, LIMIT. A visible row has every code public-recent or granted-recent, so the driver never hides a visible row (pure perf filter). SQLite has no driver (own_summary + visibility). New indexes in 0021: GIN(report_codes) WHERE own_summary, raw_reports(checked_at) WHERE visibility='public', raw_fetch_grants(tenant_id, granted_at); 0020's ix_raw_fetches_summaries is dropped (unused after this). All CONCURRENTLY.
